e6efdac115: Artist and Chicago native Peter Hurley selected over 25 Chicago musicians to be featured in this block-long mural. Musical notes are stenciled through out and as the CTA wall gets repaired, more artists will be added.
c7bd42d815: This mosaic is comprised of tile and grouting, showing leaves, snowflakes, foliage, and other seasonal elements against a yellow background. In the background, the CTA 'L' tracks and train are depicted, along with signage for Southport and Paulina stations.
e7e66fddb5: 1997. Artists Olivia Gude and Juan Angel Chavez. This amazing mural spans over 2500 sq ft across the facade of the Fellowship House. The mural explores the theme of who is an other and who is considered a fellow. The mural deals with the issue of racism in the community. The end result is serious and meaningful but also fresh, colorful and energetic. From 1997
a83bdde7f5: : Rahmaan statik Statik The Junction Grove mural is a snapshot of Englwood during the early 1900's. The overall image represents the great white flight from Englewood during the early 20th century. It also focuses on the importance of the Pullman Porters during this time. Over all the community response and perception was positive.
3da55652d5: The mural is an abstract design with representations of plants, and the river. It is predominantly red, blue, and black.
cbc23edf35: (Photo Credit: Columbia College Chicago) "The Wave" is part of a larger series called “Plastic Paradise,” which explores the relationship of man-made materials and natural landscapes. In the series, plastic bags are carefully sculpted into abstract scenes through posing and lighting. This specific image gives the illusion of depth to the building's facade while the vibrant blues bring energy to the city block. Andrea Dunn was the winner of the 2016 People’s Choice WAC mural, and also won the alumni design contest for the photo project that hangs above the new ShopColumbia.
d7cff810b5: The Undercurrent project brought art and beauty to lower Michigan Avenue with installations from three local artists. The artists were asked to create a “mirror” image of what was above below, and we are amazed by what they created. The installations can be found on the walls at The Realtors Building (Billy Goat Tavern), Intercontinental Hotel, the north wall of Grand Avenue and Michigan Avenue and serve as a brighter and safer route for commuters and visitors walking Lower Michigan Avenue. The Magnificent Mile Association secured approval from CDOT on behalf of the artist.
3b4a4d6f55: Mural is of brush and spray paint. Images consist of urban landscape with a garden theme, combined with abstract graffiti art.
f0cf4e0795: "What we create" was funded in part thru an IAP grant from DCASE. It features what women do from house care and child care to creation to keeping dreams. The faces of the women are the faces of women in the community and Elizabeth Catlett on the far right. This mural was painted in part by the campers of I Grow Chicago.
